findings.quote: They are shallow, and they hold no cloud.
findings.note: WORLD_KNOWLEDGE (blind pick A). Domain knowledge of ice-supersaturated regions -- they are geometrically thin and can be entirely clear of cloud, and are invisible from the flight deck -- decides this without the passage; C is the standard misconception and D describes contrail spreading rather than the layers. The distractors are substantive positions, so this is normal test design routed to adjudication, not a form leak.

findings.quote: After dark nothing works against the warming, since no sunlight is turned away.
findings.note: WORLD_KNOWLEDGE (blind pick D). The day/night contrail asymmetry (no shortwave albedo offset at night) is a well-known result in the field; a solver who knows it picks D and reads C as the overstated version of the same idea. A and B remain substantive operational rationales for a night-only trial, so the passage is still needed to confirm -- flag, not kill.

findings.quote: He regards the imagery as worthless and would put an end to it.
findings.note: PARTIALLY. Two options fall to form alone with no domain knowledge: D is the extreme-language option ('worthless', 'put an end to it') and C is the no-preference neutrality option, which the stem's presupposition of an attitude already disfavours. That halves the field to A/B passage-blind; A vs B genuinely needs the text.

findings.quote: It is fixed hard into the stone so that the leaf cannot move once the water rises.
findings.note: PARTIALLY (blind lean A). B is self-defeating on its face -- a pin that a leaf stands and swings on cannot be the thing that prevents the leaf moving -- and D overreaches with 'the whole of the water's push' and 'every leaf'. Both go without any domain knowledge, leaving A vs C, which the passage must still decide.

findings.quote: Because the plant was valued on its own, what a buyer paid turned mainly on the debts against the houses.
findings.note: PARTIALLY. B is eliminable blind as a category confusion (houses on a milk round do not carry debts against them) and D ends in a town-wide milk-price conclusion the stem does not ask about; neither elimination needs domain knowledge. A and C both stay live, so the passage is still required to choose.

findings.quote: Verkan var ungefär densamma, och badet krävde varken nytt avtal eller längre transport.
findings.note: PARTIALLY (blind lean A). D contradicts the stem's presupposition that the factory faced a live choice between two workable options, and A has the canonical key shape for a 'why choose X over Y' item -- comparable effect plus practical convenience. C is nevertheless a substantive rival on the size of the difference, so the passage still decides A vs C; not a kill.

findings.quote: Efterglöden var den svåraste tekniska frågan i hela tändsticksindustrin.
findings.note: PARTIALLY (blind lean C). Two options fall to form alone: A carries an industry-wide superlative that no single-factory text could support, and B a universal quantifier ('varje förändring'). That leaves the balanced two-factor C against the reductive monocausal D, and test-wiseness favours C -- materially better than chance, but D stays substantive enough that this is a flag rather than a structural-leak kill.

findings.quote: Häftena kan knappast säga något om hur planscherna faktiskt användes i klassrummen.
findings.note: PARTIALLY (blind lean A). D is pragmatically self-undermining -- a text built on the häften would not conclude that they say nothing -- and B is a reductive 'främst därför att' claim about the collection's value rather than about the guides themselves. A and C then assert mirror-image trends, so one of them is almost certainly the key; deciding between them still requires the passage.

findings.quote: Häftena kan knappast säga något om hur planscherna faktiskt användes i klassrummen.
findings.note: ARGUABLE: the text concedes this claim rather than refuting it. Bråtemo objects “Ett häfte är en önskan, säger han, och ingen vet vad läraren faktiskt sade när dörren var stängd” and the essayist herself grants it: “Det är svårt att komma runt.” The one surviving trace of actual use is null evidence — “I ett enda av dem har en lärare skrivit något i marginalen, och det som står där är ett datum.” Her rebuttal does not reclaim classroom use: “Just därför säger de något, nämligen att förändringen var avsiktlig” — i.e. publisher intent, not what happened behind the closed door. Beatable, not defensible: the case has to stop mid-paragraph at the concession and ignore the “Men bilderna förändras i takt med texterna” turn, and the prompt’s “bäst” delimiter favours key A, which is the essay’s quantified thesis (“andelen frågor sjunker från ungefär två tredjedelar till knappt en tredjedel”; “de sena planscherna har färre småting i utkanterna”). Flagged because A and D are not mutually exclusive — both agree with the text and only centrality separates them.

findings.quote: Det är svårt att komma runt.
findings.note: class 2/6: 'komma runt' in the abstract sense 'get around (an objection)' mirrors English; the settled Swedish idiom for conceding an unavoidable point is 'komma ifrån'. Native alternative: 'Det är svårt att komma ifrån.'

class 6: the collector sense in Swedish takes the particle -- 'ingen samlade pa haftena'. Bare 'samlades inte' first reads as 'were not gathered/assembled', which is not the intended sense. Native alternative: 'Ingen samlade pa dem.'

findings.quote: Där dominerade beskeden redan i de tidigaste årgångarna, och andelen frågor förblir liten hela vägen.
findings.note: class 6: tense lurch inside one sentence (preterite 'dominerade' + present 'forblir') that an editor would level out to one tense. Native alternative: '... och andelen fragor forblev liten hela vagen.'
